rule: wuuna is a declarative/main-clause marker plus third-person masculine singular subject clitic plus connective -na 'and'.
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (John Benjamins, 1999), example (155), p. 122
source_example: Axmed wuu yimii, wuuna ila hadlay.
project_execution: Require an overt preceding clause boundary; check only the encoded 3sg masculine person against exact reviewed finite morphology. Do not infer the antecedent.

rule: wayna is the reviewed way statement-clitic surface with connective -na; in the cited plural example it carries forward the plural subject and the following verb shows plural agreement.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Sarfaha Afka Soomaaliga / University of Gothenburg morphology materials, agreement example
source_example: Ardaydii ayaa soo iibsaday buugaagtii, wayna akhristeen.
project_execution: Reuse the already reviewed way person compatibility (3sg feminine or 3pl) and require exact reviewed finite morphology. Do not infer which compatible person is intended without an overt antecedent analysis.

rule: This executable stage requires wuuna/wayna/waana to begin an overt second clause after comma or semicolon. Standalone forms remain unjudged even though broader Somali usage can connect clauses without punctuation.
source: CONN-STAT-001/002/005 plus project conservative clause-boundary policy

rule: wuuna/wayna/waana are statement/declarative constructions, not focus constructions. Do not derive waadna, waanna, waydinna, or any other predicted waa+clitic+-na form from these exact records.
source: Exact source forms plus project no-paradigm-generation policy

rule: waana is the declarative sentence particle waa plus connective -na. The form itself contains no short subject pronoun, so no subject person may be inferred from waana alone.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Book 2 (University of Gothenburg, updated 4 April 2026), p. 162; R. David Zorc, Somali-English Dictionary, revised 2019, p. 527
source_example: Qoyskeennu waxa uu ka kooban yahay aabbe, hooyo iyo laba carruur ah oo ay dhaleen, waana qoys tiro yar.
project_execution: Require an overt preceding clause boundary and clause-initial waana. Recognize the connective declarative particle, but do not infer a hidden subject clitic, subject person, finite-verb agreement, or automatic rewrite.

rule: The short subject pronoun belongs to its clause, while -na links two clauses. Therefore an exact left statement clitic and exact right wuuna/wayna can be compared for same-subject compatibility without assuming that the two clauses must share one subject. Overlap supports possible continuity; disjoint person sets require discourse context rather than an automatic correction.
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (John Benjamins, 1999), example (155), p. 122; Morgan Nilsson, Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers (University of Gothenburg, 2022), pp. 8, 45
source_examples: Axmed wuu yimii, wuuna ila hadlay.
Nilsson p. 8: ordinary Somali statements normally express the subject by a pronoun even when a noun subject is present.
Nilsson p. 45: connective -na is used to connect two clauses and occurs early in the second clause.
project_execution: Compare only exact reviewed left wuu/way/waad person sets with exact reviewed right wuuna/wayna person sets. Disjoint sets produce context_required possible-subject-switch review, never an agreement error or autofix. Person-neutral waana and missing left clitic evidence remain unjudged.
